profile.reading:
Per CyrusOne's own facility page, PNW1 sits at 1025 D Street Northwest, Quincy, WA 98848, publishing 36 MW and 720,000 sq ft; CyrusOne describes it as roughly halfway between Seattle and Spokane and as the largest greenfield-built facility the company has developed in Washington state, with additional land reserved for future development subject to power availability.

Quincy, in Grant County, sits within the territory of the Grant County Public Utility District, whose low-cost hydroelectric power from Columbia River dams has drawn a dense cluster of data centers to the area from multiple operators (including Microsoft and Sabey, tracked elsewhere in this registry); CyrusOne was founded in July 2000 by David Ferdman and Larry Bursten and was taken private in 2022 when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts (KKR) and Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP) acquired the company for approximately $15 billion.

Since going private under KKR and GIP ownership in 2022, CyrusOne has continued expanding its US and international footprint; the company's own press materials cite roughly $1 billion in cumulative capital investment in its San Antonio, Texas campuses alone as of a January 2025 groundbreaking, indicating continued growth investment across its portfolio under private ownership rather than a broad slowdown following the take-private transaction.

In November 2021, KKR and GIP first announced the agreement to acquire CyrusOne in an approximately $15 billion transaction, one of the largest data center M&A deals of that period, reflecting broader private-equity and infrastructure-fund interest in colocation real estate that has also driven acquisitions of peers like QTS (by Blackstone) and CoreSite (by American Tower) around the same era; CyrusOne's current published portfolio language describes more than 50 mission-critical facilities worldwide, though the company's own site and Wikipedia give somewhat different approximate totals (over 40 versus more than 50), neither of which this registry treats as a precise, independently verified figure.
profile.facility_note: CyrusOne PNW1, Quincy, Washington: CyrusOne's largest greenfield-built Washington facility, 720,000 sq ft / 36MW, in the Grant County PUD hydroelectric-power hub.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Quincy campus publishes 36 MW of IT capacity across 720,000 square feet of technical space, the largest single disclosed data center footprint in Washington state.

This facility represents roughly 900 racks at typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack. The operator describes it as the largest greenfield facility CyrusOne has built in Washington state and notes that additional land is reserved for expansion, but explicitly constrains that expansion by power availability. This framing inverts the usual causation: the building exists and can grow, but the power grid cannot yet support it. Washington has 46 mapped data center facilities total, but only two publish power figures, so this 36 MW site accounts for 60 percent of all disclosed state capacity simply because disclosure is sparse.

The operator published no certifications or technical specifications for this facility. Whether the campus qualifies for GPU workloads, how much of the 36 MW currently serves high-density AI training versus other workloads, the amount of power needed for reserved expansion, or the timeline for that expansion remain unpublished. CyrusOne's own site does not quantify the power constraint it cites as the binding limit on growth.
